evidence.scope: Permission-mask assertion on the deployed address, CREATE2 address prediction, PoolManager authentication and canonical pool admission. It does not cover a deployment on any live chain.

test_auth_callbacksAcceptOnlyTheImmutablePoolManager and test_dep_callbacksRejectAForeignPoolManager drive every enabled callback from a foreign caller and from a substituted PoolManager and assert both are refused.

gates.note: The permission mask 0x30CC is asserted directly on the deployed hook address after a real launch, the hook constructor validates its own bits, pool admission rejects a foreign currency, a foreign tick spacing, a static-fee key and a second initialization, and every callback is asserted to accept only the immutable PoolManager.

evidence.scope: Four-quadrant swap execution through core, which rejects a wrong selector or return-data length, plus a raw-router bypass attempt that is charged identically. It does not include a dedicated malformed-selector negative test.

test_nested_hookCodeCannotReachPoolManagerSwap, test_nested_reenteringRouterIsChargedOncePerSwap and test_nested_secondUnlockInsideASwapIsRefused prove that v4's self-call callback suppression cannot be used to skip a charge.

gates.note: Selector and return-data length are enforced by Uniswap v4 core on every callback, so the passing four-quadrant suite is the executable proof. The self-call property now has a direct test: no path in the hook reaches PoolManager.swap, and a reentering router is charged exactly once.

evidence.scope: Authorization and clamping of the only input to the LP fee, plus the seat-rotation rules that bound who can move it. There is no pool-state observation to manipulate, so no same-block observation attack is modelled.
evidence.command: forge test --match-contract AuctionTest && forge test --match-contract FuzzTest

evidence.scope: test_nested_noEntryPointMovesThePoolPrice and test_auth_setLpFeeIsManagerOnly assert that no permissionless call can move the price the fee is applied against and that only the seated manager can change the fee.

gates.note: The fee input is a stored parameter of a paid role rather than a pool observation, so the manipulation surface is the role itself: only the current manager may set it, an evicted manager cannot, the value is clamped, a handover resets it to the default, and the seat can only move through the auction. The adversarial suite adds a direct assertion that no entry point moves the pool price.

evidence.scope: Bounds on write and on read, override-flag behaviour, the vacant-seat fallback and the LP-fee range invariant.
